speaker: Doctor
text: To better understand your chronic joint pain, can you tell me which specific joints are affected and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms? Additionally, do you notice any swelling, redness, or stiffness, particularly in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gout (likely with secondary osteoarthritis due to age and distribution).

I am considering gout given the involvement of the great toe, but the hip and knee pain with activity suggests osteoarthritis as well. To confirm the presence of uric acid crystals and assess joint damage, REQUEST TEST: Serum Uric Acid and REQUEST TEST: Knee_XRay. REQUEST IMAGES: Left Great Toe_XRay.
